title: 338: Ireland: Home Rule, Mutiny - and Civil War? (Part 3)

sentences.en: The dark eleventh hour draws on and sees us sold to every evil power we fought against of old.
sentences.zh: 阴暗的第十一个小时临近，我们被出卖给了我们自古以来一直抗争的每一个邪恶势力。

sentences.en: Rebellion, raping, hate, oppression, wrong and greed are loose to rule our fate by England's act and deed.
sentences.zh: 叛乱、强奸、仇恨、压迫、罪恶与贪婪，因英国的所作所为而肆虐，主宰着我们的命运。

sentences.en: We asked no more than leave to reap where we had sown, through good and ill, to cleave to our own flag and throne.
sentences.zh: 我们别无所求，只求能在耕耘之地收获，无论顺境逆境，只求忠于我们自己的旗帜与王座。

sentences.en: Now England's shot and steel beneath that flag must show how loyal hearts should kneel to England's oldest foe.
sentences.zh: 如今，英国的枪炮必须在那面旗帜下展示，忠诚的心该如何向英国最古老的敌人屈膝。

sentences.en: We know the war prepared on every peaceful home.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，每一处安宁的家园都已备战。

sentences.en: We know the hell's declared, for such as serve not Rome.
sentences.zh: 我们知道，地狱已向那些不侍奉罗马的人宣战。

sentences.en: The terror, threats and dread in market, hearth and field.
sentences.zh: 恐惧、威胁与战栗，弥漫在集市、炉边与田野。

sentences.en: We know when all is said, we perish if we yield.
sentences.zh: 我们深知，归根结底，如果我们屈服，我们必将灭亡。

sentences.en: Believe we dare not boaSt.
sentences.zh: 相信我们不敢吹嘘。

sentences.en: Believe we do not fear.
sentences.zh: 相信我们并不畏惧。

sentences.en: We stand to pay the cost in all that men hold dear.
sentences.zh: 我们挺身而出，为人们珍视的一切付出代价。

sentences.en: What answer from the north?
sentences.zh: 北方有何回应？

sentences.en: One law, one land, one throne.
sentences.zh: 同一法律，同一土地，同一王座。

sentences.en: If England drive us forth, we shall not fall alone.
sentences.zh: 如果英国将我们驱逐，我们绝不会独自倒下。

sentences.en: So, Tom Holland, that blood-curdling poem, Ulster, was written by Rudyard Kipling and published in the Morning Post on the 9th of April, 1912.
sentences.zh: 那么，汤姆·霍兰，那首令人毛骨悚然的诗《阿尔斯特》，是由鲁德亚德·吉卜林创作，并于1912年4月9日发表在《晨邮报》上的。

sentences.en: And it's a call to arms, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这是一种战斗号角，对吧？

sentences.en: By Kipling, on behalf of what he sees as the guardians of the British flame, the people of Ulster, or as we would now say, well,
sentences.zh: 这是吉卜林代表他眼中英国火种的守护者——阿尔斯特人民，或者用我们现在的话说，嗯，

sentences.en: what eventually becomes the state or statelet or province, whatever you'd like to call it, of Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 最终成为北爱尔兰这个州、小州或省份，随你怎么称呼它，所发出的号召。

sentences.en: So, here we are.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在就在这里。

sentences.en: And the civil war is approaching.
sentences.zh: 内战即将来临。

sentences.en: It is, Dominic.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，多米尼克。

sentences.en: And I think that listeners will be able to tell from that that we are now a long way from the GPO in Dublin,
sentences.zh: 我想听众们能听出来，我们现在离都柏林的邮政总局已经很远了，

sentences.en: where we were for our previous two episodes on the build-up to the Easter Rising.
sentences.zh: 那是我们前两集讨论复活节起义前奏时所在的地方。

sentences.en: Well, I probably wouldn't have read it in the GPO, Tom, to be honeSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，说实话，汤姆，我可能不会在邮政总局读这首诗。

sentences.en: I'm brave, but not that brave.
sentences.zh: 我很勇敢，但还没那么勇敢。

sentences.en: So, to explain, to remind listeners, we've done two episodes in Dublin with Paul Rouse, and now we're taking a break.
sentences.zh: 所以，解释一下，提醒听众，我们和保罗·劳斯在都柏林做了两集节目，现在我们要休息一下。

sentences.en: By magic, we have left.
sentences.zh: 像变魔术一样，我们离开了。

sentences.en: We have spirited ourselves away from the GPO, and we are now back.
sentences.zh: 我们已经从邮政总局撤离，现在回来了。

sentences.en: Where are we?
sentences.zh: 我们在哪里？

sentences.en: We're back in England.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了英国。

sentences.en: We're back in Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了利物浦。

sentences.en: We're back in Newcastle.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了纽卡斯尔。

sentences.en: We're back in the great cities of Britain.
sentences.zh: 我们回到了英国的伟大城市。

sentences.en: Edwardian Britain.
sentences.zh: 爱德华时代的英国。

sentences.en: Edwardian Britain.
sentences.zh: 爱德华时代的英国。

sentences.en: Because this story that we have framed as a story about Ireland is, of course, also a story about the other constituent parts of the United Kingdom, of Great Britain and Ireland.
sentences.zh: 因为我们将其构建为爱尔兰故事的这个叙事，当然，也是关于大不列颠及爱尔兰联合王国其他组成部分的故事。

sentences.en: And we shouldn't forget that.
sentences.zh: 我们不应忘记这一点。

sentences.en: No, we shouldn't, Tom.
sentences.zh: 是的，我们不应忘记，汤姆。

sentences.en: I mean, when we left last time,
sentences.zh: 我是说，当我们上次离开时，

sentences.en: so those of you who listened to our first two episodes in this series will know that we left last time with Paul Rouse from University College Dublin,
sentences.zh: 听过我们本系列前两集的听众会知道，上次我们离开时，都柏林大学学院的保罗·劳斯非常坚定地表示，

sentences.en: saying very firmly that at the beginning of the 1910s, the United Kingdom was, in his view, heading for a civil war, and the Great War interrupts it.
sentences.zh: 在他看来，1910年代初的联合王国正走向内战，而大战中断了这一切。

sentences.en: And, of course, we know there wasn't a civil war, but today's episode is about that civil war that never was.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们知道并没有发生内战，但今天的节目就是关于那场从未发生的内战。

sentences.en: And we're joined, Tom, by one of the great friends of the rest of history, aren't we?
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们请来了一位“历史其余部分”的老朋友，不是吗？

sentences.en: We are.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, Dan Jackson, who has appeared on two episodes, he appeared on the episode we did on the North-South Divide.
sentences.zh: 丹·杰克逊曾出现在两集节目中，他参加了我们关于南北差异的那一集。

sentences.en: He appeared on the episode we did on the beginnings of the railways.
sentences.zh: 他还参加了我们关于铁路起源的那一集。

sentences.en: He is probably best known for his wonderful, wonderful book, The Northumbrians, about the history and culture of the Northeast,
sentences.zh: 他最出名的作品可能是那本精彩绝伦的《诺森布里亚人》，讲述了东北部的历史与文化，

sentences.en: which I know both of us kind of nominated as a history book of the year back when it was published.
sentences.zh: 我知道我们俩在它出版时都把它提名为年度历史书籍。

sentences.en: But Dan has also published another book, and that book has the very, very promising title of Popular Opposition to Irish Home Rule in Edwardian Britain.
sentences.zh: 但丹还出版了另一本书，书名非常有前途，叫《爱德华时代英国对爱尔兰自治的民众反对》。

sentences.en: And, Dan, this was your doctoral subject.
sentences.zh: 丹，这就是你的博士课题。

sentences.en: So, we are absolutely now on your home territory.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们现在绝对是在你的主场。

sentences.en: Thanks very much, and thanks for the invitation again.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，也再次感谢你们的邀请。

sentences.en: Yes, and this is, you know, I was saying to Dominic before, historians go on about their period.
sentences.zh: 是的，正如我之前对多米尼克说的，历史学家总是对自己研究的时期津津乐道。

sentences.en: This is the best period.
sentences.zh: 这是最好的时期。

sentences.en: This is so fantastic.
sentences.zh: 这太棒了。

sentences.en: Such a gripping story.
sentences.zh: 这是一个如此引人入胜的故事。

sentences.en: And it has so much resonance for today, actually.
sentences.zh: 而且它对今天实际上有很大的共鸣。

sentences.en: So, I'm glad that my old thesis, published in 2009 by Liverpool University Press, and it's still available, is getting another airing.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴我那篇2009年由利物浦大学出版社出版、至今仍可买到的旧论文，能再次受到关注。

sentences.en: So, Dan, let's do the background, because in the previous episode, we were talking a lot about 19th century Ireland and about the pressures,
sentences.zh: 那么，丹，让我们来谈谈背景，因为在上一集中，我们谈了很多关于19世纪爱尔兰的情况以及压力，

sentences.en: the sense of distinctiveness, the growing pressures, the demands for Home Rule that were embodied by the Irish Parliamentary Party under John Redmond.
sentences.zh: 那种独特性感，日益增长的压力，以及约翰·雷德蒙领导下的爱尔兰议会党所体现的对自治的需求。

sentences.en: And the Liberals under Gladstone had floated Home Rule.
sentences.zh: 格莱斯顿领导下的自由党曾提出过自治。

sentences.en: Gladstone had that split his own party about it in the 1880s.
sentences.zh: 格莱斯顿在1880年代因此导致了自己的党派分裂。

sentences.en: Then they'd had another go in the 1890s, frustrated by the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 后来在1890年代他们又尝试了一次，但受到了上议院的阻挠。

sentences.en: But things all change at the end of the 1900s, don't they?
sentences.zh: 但1900年代末一切都变了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Can you give us a bit of a reminder of what's changed?
sentences.zh: 你能帮我们回顾一下发生了什么变化吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, before we get into the politics, I think there's something to be said about our general impressions about the Edwardian period.
sentences.zh: 所以，在我们进入政治之前，我认为关于我们对爱德华时代的普遍印象，有些话要说。

sentences.en: People look back kind of fondly to it.
sentences.zh: 人们回首那个时代时带着某种温情。

sentences.en: I guess it's the Downton Abbey era for some people.
sentences.zh: 我想对某些人来说，那是《唐顿庄园》的时代。

sentences.en: It's the Indian summer, Delhi Durbar, Henley Regatta.
sentences.zh: 那是印度之夏、德里杜尔巴、亨利皇家赛艇会。

sentences.en: It's cricket at the Oval.
sentences.zh: 那是椭圆球场的板球比赛。

sentences.en: It's the Kaiser at Cowes.
sentences.zh: 那是考斯的德皇。

sentences.en: Yeah, the Philip Larkin poem.
sentences.zh: 是的，菲利普·拉金的那首诗。

sentences.en: Yes, it's all that sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那种感觉。

sentences.en: It's also an era when Newcastle United are regularly champions of England.
sentences.zh: 那也是纽卡斯尔联队经常获得英格兰冠军的时代。

sentences.en: So, it's a golden age.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个黄金时代。

sentences.en: A golden age.
sentences.zh: 一个黄金时代。

sentences.en: Yeah, in many respects.
sentences.zh: 是的，在许多方面都是如此。

sentences.en: But actually, once you delve into the period, you realise that the country is, certainly by 1914, the story we're going to tell, is having a nervous breakdown.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，一旦你深入研究这个时期，你就会意识到，到1914年我们即将讲述的故事发生时，这个国家正处于神经崩溃的边缘。

sentences.en: And you see traces of that in the debates that rage around the turn of the century, that sense of foreboding that people have.
sentences.zh: 你在世纪之交激烈的辩论中可以看到这种迹象，人们心中那种不祥的预感。

sentences.en: You know, Kipling's poem, Recessional.
sentences.zh: 你知道，吉卜林的诗《退场》。

sentences.en: You know, we are masters of the universe, or are we?
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们是宇宙的主宰，还是说我们是？

sentences.en: Or are there threats looming over the horizon?
sentences.zh: 还是说地平线上正笼罩着威胁？

sentences.en: Are we as confident and prosperous and impregnable as we once were?
sentences.zh: 我们是否还像过去那样自信、繁荣且坚不可摧？

sentences.en: And that plays out in the political field through a slightly dry topic of tariff reform, which emerges as a conservative policy idea, pushed by Joseph Chamberlain, of course,
sentences.zh: 这在政治领域通过关税改革这个略显枯燥的话题表现出来，它作为一种保守党的政策理念出现，当然是由约瑟夫·张伯伦推动的，

sentences.en: a conservative politician at the time.
sentences.zh: 他当时是一位保守党政治家。

sentences.en: And it's the idea that basically we can adjust our tariff barriers to better protect our empire and encourage industrial growth in the empire and also prosperity at home.
sentences.zh: 其基本理念是，我们可以调整关税壁垒，以更好地保护我们的帝国，鼓励帝国境内的工业增长，并促进国内的繁荣。

sentences.en: But this is a massively controversial subject for a country that had set out its store politically for decades around free trade.
sentences.zh: 但这对于一个几十年来在政治上一直以自由贸易为基石的国家来说，是一个极具争议的话题。

sentences.en: And that had driven much of Britain's prosperity.
sentences.zh: 而这正是英国大部分繁荣的驱动力。

sentences.en: And so for a law after the 1860s, when Gladstone has this unfortunate period of trying to get home rule through parliament and fails, the Tories capitalise on that.
sentences.zh: 因此，在1860年代之后，当格莱斯顿经历了试图在议会通过自治法案却失败的不幸时期，保守党人利用了这一点。

sentences.en: In 1886, of course, Randolph Churchill, a leading conservative, is described as having played the orange card in his support for or opposition to Irish home rule.
sentences.zh: 当然，在1886年，保守党领袖伦道夫·丘吉尔被描述为在支持或反对爱尔兰自治的问题上打了“橙色牌”。

sentences.en: There's about two decades of Tory hegemony until the 1906 general election, which is a liberal landslide.
sentences.zh: 直到1906年大选自由党大获全胜之前，保守党统治了大约二十年。

sentences.en: And there's no sense of Irish home rule being on the on the Liberal Party's agenda in that period.
sentences.zh: 在那段时期，爱尔兰自治似乎根本不在自由党的议程上。

sentences.en: Because it doesn't need to be because, yeah, the Irish parliamentary party are not holding the balance of power.
sentences.zh: 因为它不需要在议程上，因为爱尔兰议会党并没有掌握权力平衡。

sentences.en: They need to hold the balance of power to have any influence.
sentences.zh: 他们需要掌握权力平衡才能产生任何影响。

sentences.en: But also, even so the liberals are associated with the home rule cause.
sentences.zh: 但即便如此，自由党还是与自治事业联系在一起。

sentences.en: But one thing I hadn't really gauged until you and I, Tom, both read this book, Fatal Path, by a brilliant Irish historian, Ronan Fanning, was the extent to which,
sentences.zh: 但有一件事，直到你和我，汤姆，都读了爱尔兰杰出历史学家罗南·范宁的那本《致命之路》之前，我并没有真正意识到，

sentences.en: even in the Liberal Party, which is, as it were, the more sympathetic to Irish home rule,
sentences.zh: 即使是在自由党内部，也就是所谓的对爱尔兰自治更同情的一方，

sentences.en: the people running that party are fervently anti-Catholic and have an enormous dislike of Ireland and the Irish.
sentences.zh: 运营该党的人也是狂热的反天主教徒，对爱尔兰和爱尔兰人有着巨大的厌恶。

sentences.en: Asquith, Lloyd George, especially.
sentences.zh: 阿斯奎斯，劳合·乔治，尤其是这样。

sentences.en: I mean, Lloyd George, non-conformist, he thinks Catholic priests are the devil incarnate.
sentences.zh: 我是说，劳合·乔治，作为非国教徒，他认为天主教神父是恶魔的化身。

sentences.en: He has no time for Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他根本不把爱尔兰放在眼里。

sentences.en: He thinks, you know, it's just a sort of much worse Wales.
sentences.zh: 他认为，你知道，那只是一个更糟糕的威尔士。

sentences.en: His, you know, I hadn't gauged.
sentences.zh: 他的，你知道，我之前没意识到。

sentences.en: I'd always thought there'd been some sentimental fondness for Ireland in the Liberal Party.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为自由党内部对爱尔兰有一种感性的喜爱。

sentences.en: But no, they couldn't give a damn about Ireland, could they, Dan?
sentences.zh: 但没有，他们根本不在乎爱尔兰，对吧，丹？

sentences.en: Certainly not.
sentences.zh: 当然不在乎。

sentences.en: And even when, you know, Asquith eventually becomes premier in 1908, Asquith's too busy, you know, drinking port,
sentences.zh: 即使当阿斯奎斯在1908年最终成为首相时，他太忙了，你知道，喝着波特酒，

sentences.en: playing bridge and basically texting his various girlfriends because he corresponded with them so frequently to care a damn about Ireland.
sentences.zh: 打着桥牌，基本上在给他的各个女朋友发短信，因为他与她们通信太频繁了，根本不在乎爱尔兰。

sentences.en: What changes?
sentences.zh: 什么改变了？

sentences.en: First, they have the Liberal landslide,
sentences.zh: 首先，他们经历了自由党的大胜，

sentences.en: but that majority is nibbled away in the course of the controversies around the people's budget and so on in 1909 in the confrontation with the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 但随着1909年人民预算等争议以及与上议院的对抗，多数优势被蚕食了。

sentences.en: There are two general elections in 1910 in which basically the Liberals lose their majority.
sentences.zh: 1910年举行了两次大选，自由党基本上失去了多数席位。

sentences.en: They still want to push forward their social programme and the price of that that the Irish Nationalist Party extract from them is, let's go back to Home Rule.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然想推进他们的社会计划，而爱尔兰民族党从他们那里榨取的代价是，让我们回到自治问题上。

sentences.en: We want Home Rule in return for supporting the programme of the Liberal government and getting it through Parliament.
sentences.zh: 我们想要自治，以换取支持自由党政府的计划并使其在议会通过。

sentences.en: And now there's a plausible chance that Home Rule can pass because, as we were talking with Paul last time,
sentences.zh: 现在自治通过的可能性很大，因为正如我们上次与保罗谈到的，

sentences.en: there's been this huge parliamentary reform which has removed the veto power of the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 已经进行了巨大的议会改革，取消了上议院的否决权。

sentences.en: So now, instead of blocking something, the House of Lords can only delay it by two years.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，上议院不能再阻止某事，只能将其推迟两年。

sentences.en: You have to keep the legislation unchanged, don't you?
sentences.zh: 你必须保持立法不变，对吧？

sentences.en: Unamended.
sentences.zh: 未经修正。

sentences.en: And the third time you introduce it, it will pass the House of Lords and it's through.
sentences.zh: 第三次引入时，它就会在上议院通过，从而获得通过。

sentences.en: And the Conservatives, am I right?
sentences.zh: 而保守党，我说的对吗？

sentences.en: The Conservatives see this as, I mean, they're going on all the time about the Liberals as a revolutionary committee, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 保守党认为这是，我是说，他们一直在说自由党是一个革命委员会，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, they haven't coined the phrase Bolsheviks, but they basically see the Liberals as people who are blowing up the Constitution just to stay in office.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们还没创造出“布尔什维克”这个词，但他们基本上认为自由党人是为了保住职位而炸毁宪法的人。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is a vastly controversial move on behalf of the Liberals,
sentences.zh: 是的，这是自由党方面一个极具争议的举动，

sentences.en: but they had to do something because their legislative program was consistently blocked in the Tory-dominated House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 但他们必须采取行动，因为他们的立法计划在保守党控制的上议院中不断受阻。

sentences.en: This was the last era when the landed interest had a huge political influence still in Great Britain, and they consistently did that,
sentences.zh: 这是土地利益在英国仍有巨大政治影响力的最后一个时代，他们不断这样做，

sentences.en: and they confronted the House of Lords over it, and they pushed through the Parliament Act in 1911,
sentences.zh: 他们因此与上议院对抗，并在1911年推动通过了《议会法案》，

sentences.en: which basically removed the veto of the House of Lords from legislation that came from the Commons.
sentences.zh: 该法案基本上取消了上议院对下议院立法的否决权。

sentences.en: And that opened the way to – because, of course, in the 1880s, Gladstone had the numbers to get Home Rule through the House of Commons, but not through the House of Lords.
sentences.zh: 这为——因为当然，在1880年代，格莱斯顿有足够的票数让自治法案在下议院通过，但无法通过上议院。

sentences.en: So this was a real game-changer.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个真正的游戏规则改变者。

sentences.en: And you've got David Lloyd George, famously in a speech in Newcastle, saying, you know,
sentences.zh: 大卫·劳合·乔治在纽卡斯尔的一次演讲中曾有名言，你知道，

sentences.en: the Liberal government are trying to pay for the massive armament program of building dreadnoughts and so on.
sentences.zh: 自由党政府正试图为建造无畏舰等庞大的军备计划买单。

sentences.en: And he says, you know, a duke costs as much as two dreadnoughts and lasts twice as long.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，一个公爵的造价相当于两艘无畏舰，而且寿命是其两倍。

sentences.en: So this is unheard of almost in British political history for there to be such ridicule and confrontation with the old aristocracy.
sentences.zh: 所以，在英国政治史上，对旧贵族进行如此嘲讽和对抗几乎是闻所未闻的。

sentences.en: And so a lot of Tories lose their minds over this, and some of them are called the ditchers because they're prepared to die in a ditch over Lords reform.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多保守党人对此失去了理智，其中一些人被称为“死守派”，因为他们准备为上议院改革而死守阵地。

sentences.en: But once the negotiations of the Irish Nationalist Party proceed after those two general elections, the way – the path is clear.
sentences.zh: 但一旦爱尔兰民族党的谈判在那两次大选后进行，道路——道路似乎很清楚，可以重新引入自治法案。

sentences.en: Or maybe it isn't, but the path seems to be clear to reintroduce a Home Rule bill.
sentences.zh: 或者也许并不清楚，但重新引入自治法案的道路似乎是畅通的。

sentences.en: So, Dan, if the Tories see the Liberals as kind of dangerous, subversives, communists, whatever, that fear presumably starts to radicalise the Tories.
sentences.zh: 所以，丹，如果保守党人把自由党人看作是危险的、颠覆性的、共产主义者等等，这种恐惧大概开始使保守党激进化了。

sentences.en: And they have two massive causes now.
sentences.zh: 他们现在有两个巨大的事业。

sentences.en: They're deeply upset about what's happened to the House of Lords, the degradation of the ability of the Lords to block liberal legislation.
sentences.zh: 他们对上议院发生的事情感到非常不安，即上议院阻止自由党立法的能力被削弱了。

sentences.en: So that's one thing they're very upset about.
sentences.zh: 所以这是他们非常不安的一件事。

sentences.en: But now, Hoving interview, is the issue of what Irish Home Rule, which now seems a very, very practical possibility – indeed, it's been passed, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 但现在，更重要的是爱尔兰自治的问题，这现在看起来是一个非常、非常实际的可能性——事实上，它已经通过了，不是吗？

sentences.en: It's been legislated for – what are the implications of that for the British Empire?
sentences.zh: 它已经立法了——这对大英帝国意味着什么？

sentences.en: Of course, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: And as we shall see, Ireland, especially the north of Ireland, is seen to represent the British Empire in microcosMs.
sentences.zh: 正如我们将看到的，爱尔兰，特别是爱尔兰北部，被视为大英帝国的缩影。

sentences.en: Some people describe Ireland as England stroke Britain's first colony.
sentences.zh: 有些人将爱尔兰描述为英国的第一个殖民地。

sentences.en: And so this is the first kind of chink in the armour of the British Empire.
sentences.zh: 所以这是大英帝国盔甲上的第一个裂缝。

sentences.en: This comes hot on the heels, of course, of all these debates about how do we best shore up our global dominance?
sentences.zh: 当然，这紧随所有关于我们如何最好地巩固全球统治地位的辩论之后。

sentences.en: Is tariff reform the answer?
sentences.zh: 关税改革是答案吗？

sentences.en: And those debates are still actually playing out within the Tory party in this period.
sentences.zh: 而这些辩论在这一时期实际上仍在保守党内部进行。

sentences.en: Maybe we can have another go at tariff reform and then the Irish Home Rule issue is back on the agenda.
sentences.zh: 也许我们可以再试一次关税改革，然后爱尔兰自治问题又回到了议程上。

sentences.en: And does that serve as a kind of unifying issue?
sentences.zh: 这是否起到了一种统一议题的作用？

sentences.en: I mean, is that part of why they pile in behind it?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是他们支持它的部分原因吗？

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: But I think what the most decisive factor for particularly the Conservative Party's politics in this period is a change of leadership.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这一时期保守党政治最决定性的因素是领导层的更迭。

sentences.en: Because, of course, in the years of Tory hegemony, it's Lord Salisbury.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，在保守党霸权的那些年里，掌权的是索尔兹伯里勋爵。

sentences.en: He passes on to his nephew, Arthur Balfour, hence the phrase, Bob's your uncle, of course.
sentences.zh: 他把位置传给了他的侄子亚瑟·贝尔福，当然，这就是“鲍勃是你叔叔”（Bob's your uncle，意为“事情很简单”）这个短语的由来。

sentences.en: But Arthur Balfour is a very different character.
sentences.zh: 但亚瑟·贝尔福是一个非常不同的人物。

sentences.en: He's a very – he's a man of the kind of salons of London.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非常……他是一个属于伦敦沙龙圈子的人。

sentences.en: He's a bachelor.
sentences.zh: 他是个单身汉。

sentences.en: His nickname at Oxford University was pretty fanny.
sentences.zh: 他在牛津大学时的绰号是“漂亮的范妮”。

sentences.en: Do you know my favourite Balfour aphorism, Dan?
sentences.zh: 丹，你知道我最喜欢的贝尔福格言吗？

sentences.en: Go on.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: What does he say?
sentences.zh: 他说了什么？

sentences.en: Nothing matters very much and few things matter at all.
sentences.zh: “没什么事很重要，几乎没什么事值得在意。”

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So he wasn't exactly the dynamic leader that the Tories needed.
sentences.zh: 所以他并不是保守党所需要的那种充满活力的领导人。

sentences.en: He's not going to die in a ditch, is he?
sentences.zh: 他可不会为了什么事去拼命，对吧？

sentences.en: He's not going to die in a ditch.
sentences.zh: 他不会去拼命的。

sentences.en: So they cast around a bit and they have some internal debates.
sentences.zh: 所以他们四处物色，并进行了一些内部辩论。

sentences.en: And the man they come up with as their leader is Andrew Bonner Law, who until Boris Johnson came along was the only British Prime Minister,
sentences.zh: 他们选出的领导人是安德鲁·博纳·劳，在鲍里斯·约翰逊出现之前，他是唯一一位英国首相，

sentences.en: because he becomes Prime Minister in the 1920s, to be born outside of the United Kingdom.
sentences.zh: 因为他在20世纪20年代成为首相，但他出生在英国本土之外。

sentences.en: He was born in New Brunswick, the back of beyond New Brunswick, to a Presbyterian minister, and he's got this Ulster and Scottish background.
sentences.zh: 他出生在新不伦瑞克，新不伦瑞克偏远的地方，父亲是一位长老会牧师，他有着阿尔斯特和苏格兰的背景。

sentences.en: And that's the key.
sentences.zh: 这就是关键所在。

sentences.en: That's the key factor here.
sentences.zh: 这是这里的关键因素。

sentences.en: I was about to say, Dan, that's the key, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 我正想说，丹，这就是关键，不是吗？

sentences.en: Because I opened with that Kipling poem Ulster.
sentences.zh: 因为我开场时引用了吉卜林的诗《阿尔斯特》。

sentences.en: And we haven't – in all of this, Tom – we haven't talked very much about the situation in the north of the island of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 而且汤姆，在所有这些讨论中，我们还没有过多谈论爱尔兰岛北部的情况。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So that's the key thing, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以那是关键所在，不是吗？

sentences.en: But Paul described the plantations.
sentences.zh: 但保罗描述了那些殖民地。

sentences.en: So in the 16th and 17th century, all these settlers arriving, including Cromwell's troops, who are fervently Protestant, often of Scottish heritage.
sentences.zh: 所以在16和17世纪，所有这些定居者抵达，包括克伦威尔的军队，他们是狂热的新教徒，通常具有苏格兰血统。

sentences.en: And they, Dan – I mean, they are the – this is where the issue becomes, as it were, incendiary, sometimes literally incendiary,
sentences.zh: 丹，我的意思是，他们是……这就是问题变得——怎么说呢——具有煽动性，有时甚至是字面意义上的煽动性的地方，

sentences.en: because they are concentrated in the northeastern corner of the island of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 因为他们集中在爱尔兰岛的东北角。

sentences.en: And some of them, many of them, can trace their – you know, they're not settlers now.
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人，许多人，可以追溯他们的……你知道，他们现在已经不是定居者了。

sentences.en: They can trace their lineage back centuries, can't they?
sentences.zh: 他们可以把血统追溯到几个世纪前，不是吗？

sentences.en: I mean, as far as they're concerned, they've built – I mean, Kipling says in this sort of poem, they want to reap where they had sown.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就他们而言，他们已经建立了……吉卜林在这首诗里说，他们想在播种的地方收获。

sentences.en: They had created this world.
sentences.zh: 他们创造了这个世界。

sentences.en: And they are terrified of Irish home rule, because they think they will be governed by a Catholic majority on the island of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他们对爱尔兰自治感到恐惧，因为他们认为自己将被爱尔兰岛上的天主教多数派统治。

sentences.en: That's right, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那是对的，不是吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And as I know you've discussed on many occasions, on different topics on this podcast,
sentences.zh: 正如我知道你在本播客的不同主题中多次讨论过的那样，

sentences.en: it's important for us to get back into the mindset of an era when debates about how you did Christianity were still really important.
sentences.zh: 我们有必要回到那个时代的心态，当时关于如何实践基督教的辩论仍然非常重要。

sentences.en: Because this is basically the last time that religion matters in British political history, I would argue, before the First World War,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为，这是第一次世界大战前，宗教在英国政治史上真正重要的最后时期，

sentences.en: because it coalesces around the cause of Ulster and not being seen to betray these loyal Protestant subjects and hand them over, as it's seen, to a disloyal and Roman Catholic.
sentences.zh: 因为它围绕着阿尔斯特的事业凝聚起来，不被视为背叛这些忠诚的新教臣民，也不被视为将他们移交给一个不忠诚的罗马天主教徒。

sentences.en: And this is still an era when prejudice against Roman Catholics is massive, widespread, and very often violent.
sentences.zh: 而且这仍然是一个对罗马天主教徒的偏见巨大、普遍且往往非常暴力的时代。

sentences.en: It dumbfounds people.
sentences.zh: 这让人们感到震惊。

sentences.en: It dumbfounds people in the Tory party.
sentences.zh: 这让保守党内的人感到震惊。

sentences.en: But the guy who galvanizes that anger into a political program is Andrew Bonner-Law.
sentences.zh: 但将这种愤怒转化为政治纲领的人是安德鲁·博纳·劳。

sentences.en: He's known as Bonner.
sentences.zh: 他被称为博纳。

sentences.en: He was his middle name, so he's known as Bonner-Law.
sentences.zh: 那是他的中间名，所以他被称为博纳·劳。

sentences.en: He's described as Law often in the papers at the time.
sentences.zh: 当时的报纸经常称他为劳。

sentences.en: It wasn't a double-barreled name.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个双姓。

sentences.en: But he's absolutely critical here because he is so hardcore.
sentences.zh: 但他在这里绝对至关重要，因为他非常强硬。

sentences.en: He's a former Glasgow iron merchant.
sentences.zh: 他曾是格拉斯哥的钢铁商人。

sentences.en: He's been an MP in Glasgow and Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 他曾是格拉斯哥和利物浦的议员。

sentences.en: And they're basically the two most sectarian cities in Britain.
sentences.zh: 而这两个城市基本上是英国宗派主义最严重的城市。

sentences.en: So he knows the emotions that this issue can cause on kind of Edwardian street politics.
sentences.zh: 所以他了解这个问题在爱德华时代的街头政治中可能引发的情绪。

sentences.en: And this is basically the issue that the Tory party had been casting around for a substantive issue to confront the Liberals with, a vote winner.
sentences.zh: 这基本上是保守党一直在寻找的实质性议题，用来对抗自由党，一个能赢得选票的议题。

sentences.en: This is what they settle on.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们最终确定的议题。

sentences.en: And this is how it plays out for the next few years.
sentences.zh: 这就是它在接下来几年里的发展方式。

sentences.en: But for Law, or I mean, I know people call him Bonner-Law now.
sentences.zh: 但对于劳，或者说，我知道人们现在叫他博纳·劳。

sentences.en: By the time you said people called him Law.
sentences.zh: 在你刚才说人们叫他劳的时候。

sentences.en: It's not just a cynical manoeuvre, is it?
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是一种愤世嫉俗的策略，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, he'd lost his father, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想他失去了他的父亲。

sentences.en: His father had moved back to Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲搬回了北爱尔兰。

sentences.en: He had spent a lot of time travelling to see his father.
sentences.zh: 他花了很多时间去探望他的父亲。

sentences.en: He was, biographers sort of say, when his father died, he was prostrate with grief.
sentences.zh: 传记作者说，当他父亲去世时，他悲痛欲绝。

sentences.en: He swore to uphold his father's legacy, all of this stuff.
sentences.zh: 他发誓要维护他父亲的遗产，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: I mean, for Bonner-Law, who, as you said, is a really hard man, quite a doer man.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，对于博纳·劳来说，正如你所说，他是一个非常强硬的人，一个实干家。

sentences.en: Oh, very much so, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，非常确实，是的。

sentences.en: This is really, really passionate kind of stuff, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这真的是非常充满激情的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: It is completely.
sentences.zh: 完全是这样。

sentences.en: I don't want to give the impression that it was just a cynical manoeuvre, by any means, because this was important to people.
sentences.zh: 我绝不想给人留下这仅仅是一种愤世嫉俗的策略的印象，因为这对人们来说很重要。

sentences.en: But Bonner-Law spotted this in a way that someone like Arthur Balfour, I would suggest, couldn't really see the passions that this could engender, and did.
sentences.zh: 但博纳·劳以一种我认为像亚瑟·贝尔福那样的人无法真正看到这种激情可能引发的方式发现了这一点，并且确实做到了。

sentences.en: But it did require someone to stoke the flames of anger.
sentences.zh: 但这确实需要有人来煽动愤怒的火焰。

sentences.en: And it was through the work of Bonner-Law, working hand in glove with the leadership of the Ulster Unionists,
sentences.zh: 正是通过博纳·劳的工作，与阿尔斯特统一党领导层紧密合作，

sentences.en: as we'll go on to discuss, that really tipped this country very closely towards a conflagration on the outbreak of the First World War.
sentences.zh: 正如我们接下来要讨论的那样，这确实使这个国家在第一次世界大战爆发时非常接近一场大火。

sentences.en: So, Dan, you mentioned there the leadership of the Ulster Unionists.
sentences.zh: 那么，丹，你提到了阿尔斯特统一党的领导层。

sentences.en: So, we've been hearing how the Irish Parliamentary Party,
sentences.zh: 所以，我们一直在听爱尔兰议会党的情况，

sentences.en: Enthusiasts for Home Rule, I mean, the whole point of them is that they are parliamentary.
sentences.zh: 自治的支持者，我的意思是，他们的全部意义在于他们是议会制的。

sentences.en: They are working through constitutional means.
sentences.zh: 他们通过宪法手段工作。

sentences.en: Do the Ulster Unionists have a constitutional approach, a possibility of blocking Home Rule, or are they absolutely set on pushing it, even to the degree of violence,
sentences.zh: 阿尔斯特统一党是否有宪法途径，有阻止自治的可能性，还是他们绝对决心推动它，甚至达到暴力的程度，

sentences.en: of kind of setting up paramilitary opposition?
sentences.zh: 建立准军事反对派？

sentences.en: Basically, yes, because they can see the logic of the Parliament Act having been enacted, that there isn't the House of Lords bulwark to protect them anymore after 1911.
sentences.zh: 基本上是的，因为他们能看出《议会法案》颁布后的逻辑，即1911年后不再有上议院作为保护他们的堡垒。

sentences.en: So, when, on 11th of April 1912, Herbert Asquith introduces the third Home Rule Bill to Parliament, they know that the writing's on the wall.
sentences.zh: 所以，当赫伯特·阿斯奎斯于1912年4月11日向议会提交第三份《自治法案》时，他们知道大势已去。

sentences.en: There are very limited parliamentary obstacles in its way now.
sentences.zh: 现在阻碍它的议会障碍非常有限。

sentences.en: And so, they start to mobilise in every possible sense.
sentences.zh: 因此，他们开始在各个方面进行动员。

sentences.en: And one of the first things they do is that they select a man called Sir Edward Carson as their leader.
sentences.zh: 他们做的第一件事就是选择了一个叫爱德华·卡森爵士的人作为他们的领导人。

sentences.en: Now, Carson is an absolutely fascinating figure.
sentences.zh: 现在，卡森是一个绝对迷人的人物。

sentences.en: He's probably better known these days because he had a glittering career in the law.
sentences.zh: 如今他可能更出名，因为他在法律界有着辉煌的职业生涯。

sentences.en: He's probably one of the best-paid barristers in the country, millionaire in that period.
sentences.zh: 他可能是全国收入最高的律师之一，在那个时期是百万富翁。

sentences.en: He took on a range of very famous cases.
sentences.zh: 他处理了一系列非常著名的案件。

sentences.en: Probably the most famous one, though, was when he defended the Marquess of Queensbury against Oscar Wilde's accusation of libel in 1895, I think it was.
sentences.zh: 不过最著名的可能是在1895年，我想是那一年，他为昆斯伯里侯爵辩护，对抗奥斯卡·王尔德的诽谤指控。

sentences.en: Because they'd been at school together, hadn't they, in Dublin?
sentences.zh: 因为他们曾在都柏林一起上学，不是吗？

sentences.en: They'd gone to Trinity College Dublin together.
sentences.zh: 他们一起去了都柏林三一学院。

sentences.en: They both came from that Anglo-Irish ascendancy Dublin world.
sentences.zh: 他们都来自那个盎格鲁-爱尔兰统治阶级的都柏林世界。

sentences.en: And interestingly, Edward Carson is the Unionist MP for Dublin University.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，爱德华·卡森是都柏林大学的统一党议员。

sentences.en: Because this is still the era when the top universities sent MPs to Parliament.
sentences.zh: 因为这仍然是顶尖大学向议会派遣议员的时代。

sentences.en: So, Oxford and Cambridge, the Scottish universities, UCL, and Dublin University sent two MPs.
sentences.zh: 所以，牛津和剑桥、苏格兰的大学、伦敦大学学院和都柏林大学各派两名议员。

sentences.en: And Carson was one of them.
sentences.zh: 而卡森就是其中之一。

sentences.en: Because Dublin in this period, I mean, you explored it.
sentences.zh: 因为这一时期的都柏林，我的意思是，你探索过它。

sentences.en: It's a Georgian city in many respects.
sentences.zh: 它在许多方面是一座乔治亚风格的城市。

sentences.en: It's where Dublin Castle is located.
sentences.zh: 都柏林城堡就坐落在这里。

sentences.en: And it's still a pretty Unionist city in many respects.
sentences.zh: 而且在许多方面，它仍然是一座相当统一主义的城市。

sentences.en: And there's an Irish insult that's occasionally used for Dubliners to call them Jackenes,
sentences.zh: 有一个爱尔兰侮辱性词汇偶尔用来称呼都柏林人，叫“杰克尼”（Jackeens），

sentences.en: which is said to come from the fact that they wave Union Jacks around, or used to, at leaSt.

sentences.zh: “我一直希望爱尔兰的天主教徒能自治，”埃舍勋爵写信给玛戈·阿斯奎斯说。

sentences.zh: “几个世纪以来，事实证明我们不适合统治一个天主教社区。”

sentences.zh: “但我们统治天主教徒的不适程度，还不及他们统治新教社区的一半。”

sentences.en: That is the whole ethical and political aspect of the situation.
sentences.zh: 这就是整个局势在伦理和政治层面的核心。

sentences.zh: 正如丹尼尔·杰克逊所观察到的，1912年至1914年的地方自治危机，是宗教与政治在英国政坛最后一次产生严重交集。

sentences.zh: 是的，很高兴听到这个。

sentences.en: where the King had to pledge to uphold the Protestant reform, reformed religion, the governance of the Church of Scotland and all this business,

sentences.en: God, it's carnage.

sentences.en: Britain is, for all the jitteriness about the Boer War and national degeneracy and all this sort of carry on that you get in the Edwardian period,

sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为它结合了几个非常有趣的观点。

sentences.en: And that added a kind of piquancy to these questions that had been fundamental to British national identity from the kind of late 1500s onwards,

sentences.en: And that's exactly what the Tory Unionist parties that were widely known in that period do.
sentences.zh: 而这正是那个时期广为人知的保守党统一派所做的。

sentences.en: And so isn't that the paradox that the people encouraging paramilitary displays in British cities and villages, the people who are seriously proposing that the army,
sentences.zh: 那么，这难道不是一个悖论吗？那些在英国城市和村庄鼓励准军事展示的人，那些认真提议军队，

sentences.en: rather than be sent to intervene, should potentially mutiny,
sentences.zh: 而不是被派去干预，反而应该潜在地哗变的人，

sentences.en: that the people doing this are the avowed defenders of the Constitution, the Tories, the Conservatives, the people who, by definition, oppose the kind of radical solutions.
sentences.zh: 这些人竟然是宪法的公开捍卫者，是托利党人，是保守党人，是那些按理说反对激进解决方案的人。

sentences.en: But, Tom, just to jump in for a second, I know what my answer to that would be, which is that, I mean, you see it in their speeches, Andrew Bonner Law's speeches.
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，插一句，我知道我的答案是什么，我的意思是，你在他们的演讲中，在安德鲁·博纳·劳的演讲中就能看到。

sentences.en: He would say, through a terrible stroke of misfortune, power has been seized by a cynical group of revolutionaries, Asquith, Lloyd George.
sentences.zh: 他会说，由于一场可怕的不幸，权力被一群愤世嫉俗的革命者——阿斯奎斯、劳合·乔治——夺取了。

sentences.en: We are just taking up arms to defend.
sentences.zh: 我们只是拿起武器进行自卫。

sentences.en: He would say we're defending the Constitution, wouldn't he, Dan?
sentences.zh: 他会说我们在捍卫宪法，不是吗，丹？

sentences.en: Yeah, he would, and he makes a famous speech at Blenheim Palace in late 1912, the gist of which is, I can think of no length of resistance that Ulster would go,
sentences.zh: 是的，他会这么说，他在1912年底在布伦海姆宫发表了一场著名的演讲，大意是，我想不出阿尔斯特会采取什么程度的抵抗，

sentences.en: that they wouldn't either be justified in doing, and that we won't support them in doing.
sentences.zh: 是他们不该做的，而我们不支持他们去做的。

sentences.en: This is still at this ambiguous phase I mentioned earlier.
sentences.zh: 这仍然处于我之前提到的那个模糊阶段。

sentences.en: But even when the Ulster Volunteer Forces inaugurated in early 1913, around the time, by the way, that Carson, Edward Carson,
sentences.zh: 但即使在1913年初阿尔斯特志愿部队成立时，顺便说一下，大约在卡森，爱德华·卡森，

sentences.en: introduces in Parliament an amendment to the Home Rule Bill to exclude all nine counties of the historic province of Ulster,
sentences.zh: 在议会提出一项对《地方自治法案》的修正案，旨在排除历史上的阿尔斯特省全部九个郡的时候，

sentences.en: that eventually becomes six counties after the First World War.
sentences.zh: 那在第一次世界大战后最终变成了六个郡。

sentences.en: Because the Ulster Unionists don't want their three extras that have lots of Catholics, do they?
sentences.zh: 因为阿尔斯特统一派不想要那三个拥有大量天主教徒的额外郡，对吧？

sentences.en: Because they think they won't be able to govern.
sentences.zh: 因为他们认为自己无法统治。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They want to make sure that the portion of Ulster has an inbuilt Protestant majority to safeguard their position.
sentences.zh: 他们想确保阿尔斯特的那部分拥有内在的新教多数，以保障他们的地位。

sentences.en: But that's a bitter pill for Carson to swallow, of course, because he could say that this will leave the Southern Unionists,
sentences.zh: 但这对卡森来说当然是一颗苦果，因为他可以说这将抛弃南方统一派，

sentences.en: of which there are still quite a lot in places like Dublin, even Cork, Galway and other places in urban Ireland.
sentences.zh: 在都柏林、甚至科克、戈尔韦和爱尔兰城市地区的其他地方，仍然有相当多的南方统一派。

sentences.en: There are still quite a number of Unionists, but they don't have the numbers really, and they're too disparate.
sentences.zh: 仍然有相当多的统一派，但他们的人数确实不够，而且太分散了。

sentences.en: It's all about Ulster from 1913.
sentences.zh: 从1913年起，一切都围绕着阿尔斯特。

sentences.en: But Dan, just to follow up on that idea of the Tories as being the radicals, I mean, I hear what Dominic says, but just to quote you what Ronan Fanning says about Boner Law,
sentences.zh: 但是丹，接着刚才关于托利党是激进分子的观点，我的意思是，我听到了多米尼克的说法，但我想引用罗南·范宁关于博纳·劳的评价，

sentences.en: he describes Boner Law leading the Conservative and Unionist Party to embrace a policy of revolution without parallel in modern British history.
sentences.zh: 他描述博纳·劳带领保守党和统一党采取了一种现代英国历史上前所未有的革命政策。

sentences.en: Do you think he's right about that?
sentences.zh: 你认为他对此评价正确吗？

sentences.en: Completely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: I think it's because the Tories in this period are completely boxed in.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是因为托利党在这一时期完全陷入了困境。

sentences.en: Their support for the Constitution, if I was being cynical,
sentences.zh: 如果我愤世嫉俗一点的话，他们对宪法的支持，

sentences.en: is entirely provisional on it conforming to their understanding what the Constitution should look like and not up for amendment via the democratic process.
sentences.zh: 完全取决于宪法是否符合他们对宪法应有样子的理解，而不是通过民主程序进行修正。

sentences.en: And so they're quite willing, brazenly willing, to support the Ulster Volunteer Force.
sentences.zh: 所以他们非常愿意，厚颜无耻地愿意支持阿尔斯特志愿部队。

sentences.en: And there are really prominent Conservative politicians, if I can introduce one name here, an absolutely massive lad called F.E.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有非常著名的保守党政客，如果我可以介绍一个名字的话，一个绝对重量级的人物，叫F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: Dan, you've made me so happy that you've mentioned F.E.
sentences.zh: 丹，你提到F.E.让我太高兴了。

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: F.E.
sentences.zh: F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: I mean, he is quite yet another barrister.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他又是另一位大律师。

sentences.en: And I always think this is bad news for a nation's polity when barristers are prominently involved in the political scene.
sentences.zh: 我一直认为，当大律师们显著参与政治舞台时，这对一个国家的政体来说不是好消息。

sentences.en: But F.E.
sentences.zh: 但F.E.

sentences.en: Smith, another extraordinarily wealthy, dazzling Oxford scholar, but he's a Liverpool Tory MP.
sentences.zh: 史密斯，另一位极其富有、令人眼花缭乱的牛津学者，但他是一位利物浦的托利党议员。

sentences.en: And he understands what all this means.
sentences.zh: 他明白这一切意味着什么。

sentences.en: And Liverpool in this period is absolutely central to this story.
sentences.zh: 而利物浦在这一时期对这个故事绝对是核心。

sentences.en: It's where Carson goes after signing the covenant.
sentences.zh: 那是卡森签署盟约后去的地方。

sentences.en: He sails across the Irish Sea.
sentences.zh: 他横渡爱尔兰海。

sentences.en: The Liverpool Courier has this enormous headline, Liverpool's sister of BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 《利物浦信使报》有这样一个巨大的标题：“利物浦是贝尔法斯特的姐妹”。

sentences.en: And Liverpool is still this kind of sectarian cauldron.
sentences.zh: 而利物浦仍然是这种宗派主义的温床。

sentences.en: In 1910, the elections of 1910, nine out of the 11 Merseyside seats are held by unionists, one by a liberal.
sentences.zh: 1910年，1910年的选举中，默西塞德郡11个席位中有9个由统一派把持，1个由自由党把持。

sentences.en: And the other one is held by an Irish nationalist, T.P.
sentences.zh: 另一个由爱尔兰民族主义者T.P.

sentences.en: O'Connor, the only Irish nationalist MP outside of the island of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 奥康纳把持，他是爱尔兰岛以外唯一的爱尔兰民族主义议员。

sentences.en: This is how unique this city is.
sentences.zh: 这就是这座城市的独特之处。

sentences.en: And I often think that Liverpool's tradition as England's most Tory city, which it was until right until the 1970s, has been completely airbrushed out of that city's understanding.
sentences.zh: 我经常认为，利物浦作为英国最保守城市的传统——直到20世纪70年代一直如此——已经完全从该城市的认知中被抹去了。

sentences.en: Yeah, they don't go on about that now.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们现在不怎么提那个了。

sentences.en: No, no, the idea that a crowd of Liverpool supporters would boo the national anthem as they were doing recently would be mind-boggling, even as recently as the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 不，不，利物浦球迷嘘国歌的想法，就像他们最近做的那样，即使在20世纪50年代也是不可思议的。

sentences.en: But Liverpool's political tradition was partly shaped by its economic base, which is largely landlordism in terms of dockside rather than productive industries like Manchester was.
sentences.zh: 但利物浦的政治传统部分是由其经济基础塑造的，主要是码头区的地主制，而不是像曼彻斯特那样的生产性工业。

sentences.en: The presence nearby of the landed interest through the earls of Derby, who were still very influential in British politics,
sentences.zh: 德比伯爵家族通过土地利益在附近的存在，他们当时在英国政坛仍然非常有影响力，

sentences.en: but chiefly the growth of a native orange tradition in Liverpool, which was massive and largely prompted by a kind of backlash vote.
sentences.zh: 但主要是利物浦本土奥兰治传统的增长，这非常庞大，很大程度上是由一种反弹投票所推动的。

sentences.en: But anyway, I mentioned F.E.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，我提到了F.E.

sentences.en: Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯。

sentences.en: He gets the nickname Galloper Smith because he acts as the sort of Carson's ADC,
sentences.zh: 他得到了“飞奔的史密斯”这个绰号，因为他充当了卡森的副官，

sentences.en: riding around on horseback at UVF parades and manoeuvres and so on in Northern Ireland throughout 1913 and 14.
sentences.zh: 在1913年和1914年期间，骑着马在北爱尔兰的UVF游行和演习中四处奔走。

sentences.en: Quite brazenly supporting basically armed rebellion against the British government.
sentences.zh: 公然支持基本上针对英国政府的武装叛乱。

sentences.en: Dan, I think you've sold F.E.
sentences.zh: 丹，我觉得你把F.E.

sentences.en: Smith a tiny bit short by describing him as this incredibly charismatic and dashing barrister because he's actually probably the greatest wit, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 史密斯描述为这位极其有魅力和潇洒的大律师，有点低估他了，因为他实际上可能是最伟大的智者，不是吗？

sentences.en: Or one of the two or three greatest wits.
sentences.zh: 或者两三个最伟大的智者之一。

sentences.en: So he was Churchill's great hero.
sentences.zh: 所以他是丘吉尔心目中的大英雄。

sentences.en: Tom, I'm going to read you some F.E.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我要给你读一些F.E.

sentences.en: Smith quotes.
sentences.zh: 史密斯的名言。

sentences.en: Is this the wit and wisdom of F.E.
sentences.zh: 这是F.E.

sentences.en: Smith?
sentences.zh: 史密斯的才智与智慧吗？

sentences.en: Exactly, by Winston Churchill and his great contemporaries.
sentences.zh: 没错，出自温斯顿·丘吉尔和他那些伟大的同时代人之手。

sentences.en: So when F.E.
sentences.zh: 所以当F.E.

sentences.en: Smith was a young barrister, he was up in front of a man called Judge Willis.
sentences.zh: 史密斯还是一名年轻的大律师时，他曾站在一位名叫威利斯法官的人面前。

sentences.en: And Judge Willis said to him, Mr. Smith, have you ever heard of a saying by Bacon, the great Bacon, that youth and discretion are ill-witted companions?
sentences.zh: 威利斯法官对他说：史密斯先生，你是否听说过培根——那位伟大的培根——说过的一句话：青春与谨慎是格格不入的伙伴？

sentences.en: And F.E.
sentences.zh: 而F.E.

sentences.en: Smith said, yes, I have.
sentences.zh: 史密斯回答说：是的，我听说过。

sentences.en: And have you, sir, ever heard of a saying by Bacon, the great Bacon, that a much-talking judge is like an ill-tuned symbol?
sentences.zh: 那么先生，你是否也听说过培根——那位伟大的培根——说过的一句话：喋喋不休的法官就像走调的钹？

sentences.en: And the judge at that said to him, you are extremely offensive, young man.
sentences.zh: 法官听后对他说：年轻人，你真是极其无礼。

sentences.en: And F.E.
sentences.zh: 而F.E.

sentences.en: Smith said, in open court, as a matter of fact, we both are, but I am trying to be and you can't help it.
sentences.zh: 史密斯在公开法庭上说：事实上，我们两个都很无礼，但我是在努力表现得无礼，而你是天生如此，改也改不掉。

sentences.en: But even better than that is he was talking to a high court judge who was presiding in a case of a man who'd been accused of sodomy.
sentences.zh: 但比这更精彩的是，他曾与一位高等法院法官交谈，当时法官正在审理一名被控鸡奸罪的男子的案件。

sentences.en: And the high court judge said to F.E.
sentences.zh: 高等法院法官对F.E.

sentences.en: Smith, could you tell me what do you think one ought to give a man who allows himself to be buggered?
sentences.zh: 史密斯说：你能告诉我，你认为对于一个允许自己被鸡奸的人，应该判处什么刑罚吗？

sentences.en: And F.E.
sentences.zh: 而F.E.

sentences.en: Smith said, oh, 30 shillings or two pounds, whatever you happen to have on you.
sentences.zh: 史密斯回答说：哦，30先令或者两英镑吧，看你身上正好带了多少。

sentences.en: But that's the kind of joke that if Carson had been listening to it, he'd have got F.E.
sentences.zh: 但那种笑话，如果卡森当时听到了，他会把F.E.

sentences.en: Smith sent to Reading Jail for 10 years or whatever.
sentences.zh: 史密斯送进雷丁监狱关上10年或者更久。

sentences.en: And F.E.
sentences.zh: 而F.E.

sentences.en: Smith plays up to his – he was Churchill's great drinking buddy, even though Churchill's a liberal in this period.
sentences.zh: 史密斯充分利用了他的特质——他是丘吉尔伟大的酒友，尽管丘吉尔在那个时期是自由党人。

sentences.en: Smith's a Tory.
sentences.zh: 而史密斯是保守党人。

sentences.en: He's making – F.E.
sentences.zh: 他在做演讲——F.E.

sentences.en: is making a speech somewhere and he says – it's about the liberals' kind of welfare program.
sentences.zh: 在某个地方发表演讲，他说——内容是关于自由党那种福利计划的。

sentences.en: And he says something like, I see Mr. Churchill has stolen the socialists' clothes while they were bathing, if they do bathe, which I doubt.
sentences.zh: 他说了一些类似这样的话：我看到丘吉尔先生趁社会主义者洗澡时偷走了他们的衣服，如果他们真的洗澡的话，对此我深表怀疑。

sentences.en: So he's full of little quips like that.
sentences.zh: 所以他满嘴都是这种小俏皮话。

sentences.en: But he's another charismatic figure.
sentences.zh: 但他也是另一位极具魅力的人物。

sentences.en: I think – I remember discussing with the great professor Roy Foster once about – doyenne of Irish historians in many ways – about Edward Carson.
sentences.zh: 我记得曾与伟大的罗伊·福斯特教授讨论过——他在许多方面都是爱尔兰历史学界的泰斗——关于爱德华·卡森的话题。

sentences.en: And he said, Carson, you know, he had a certain sexual charisma that was well noted by not just female voters, I would imagine,
sentences.zh: 他说，卡森，你知道，他有一种独特的性魅力，我想不仅是女性选民注意到了这一点，

sentences.en: but particularly female voters who were just kind of all of a quiver whenever he appeared.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些女性选民，每当他出现时，她们总是心潮澎湃。

sentences.en: And some people have seen a kind of – a premonition of a sort of almost fascist vibe.
sentences.zh: 有些人从中看到了一种——某种近乎法西斯氛围的预兆。

sentences.en: I don't think that – it's quite right.
sentences.zh: 我不认为那种说法完全正确。

sentences.en: But I think there is something in the strong man, the mass rallies, the arc lights.
sentences.zh: 但我认为在强人、群众集会和聚光灯中确实存在某种东西。

sentences.en: The paramilitaries marching up and down.
sentences.zh: 准军事部队在走来走去。

sentences.en: So, I mean, this is the age of the Boy Scout movement, I suppose.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，我想这大概是童子军运动的时代。

sentences.en: But it's also the age when there's an absolute fascination.
sentences.zh: 但这也是一个充满绝对迷恋的时代。

sentences.en: I mean, Tom, we did that podcast about King Solomon's Mines, published, what, 20 years earlier?
sentences.zh: 我是说，汤姆，我们做过那期关于《所罗门王的宝藏》的播客，那是早了20年出版的吧？

sentences.en: Obsession with manliness, with brotherhood, with people in tight trousers, riding up and down, promising civil wars.
sentences.zh: 对男子气概、兄弟情谊的痴迷，还有穿着紧身裤的人，骑着马走来走去，承诺要发动内战。

sentences.en: But specifically, this idea of Carson and F.E.
sentences.zh: 但具体来说，这种关于卡森和F.E.

sentences.en: Smith as kind of charismatic, almost sexually charged leaders,
sentences.zh: 史密斯作为那种充满魅力、几乎带有性张力的领导人的想法，

sentences.en: these are not the kind of people, I imagine, that Asquith, for instance, would particularly understand, would particularly have a handle on.
sentences.zh: 我想这并不是阿斯奎斯之流能够特别理解、特别能掌控的那种人。

sentences.en: So if Asquith doesn't understand the emotions that are being stirred up in Ulster, the religious motions,
sentences.zh: 所以如果阿斯奎斯不理解阿尔斯特地区正在激起的情绪，那些宗教情绪，

sentences.en: presumably also he's constitutionally incapable of understanding what the potential kind of power of people like Carson and Smith is as well.
sentences.zh: 想必他在宪法上也无法理解像卡森和史密斯这样的人所拥有的潜在力量。

sentences.en: I mean, does he just simply not appreciate the scale of the crisis that he's building?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他难道真的没有意识到他正在制造的危机规模吗？

sentences.en: I think he appreciates the crisis, but I just don't think he knows what to do about it.
sentences.zh: 我认为他意识到了危机，但我只是觉得他不知道该怎么处理。

sentences.en: You see a bit of that in the First World War.
sentences.zh: 你在第一次世界大战中也能看到这一点。

sentences.en: There's a famous line, because, you know, he was quite a laid-back figure, to say the least, when he meets some society aristocratic lady who says to him, this is about 1915 or 16,
sentences.zh: 有一句名言，因为你知道，他是个相当悠闲的人，至少可以这么说，当他遇到一位上流社会的贵族女士时，她说——这大约是在1915或16年——

sentences.en: he said, Mr. Asquith, do you take an interest in the war?
sentences.zh: 她说：阿斯奎斯先生，你关心这场战争吗？

sentences.en: You know, because he's...
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为他……

sentences.en: That's the dynamic leadership that Britain needs.
sentences.zh: 这就是英国所需要的充满活力的领导力。

sentences.en: So does he take an interest in Ulster?
sentences.zh: 那么他关心阿尔斯特问题吗？

sentences.en: I think he basically...
sentences.zh: 我想他基本上……

sentences.en: Asquith basically wishes it would all just go away.
sentences.zh: 阿斯奎斯基本上希望这一切都能自动消失。

sentences.en: You know, he's not the charismatic stump speaker that Carson or Smith, or even Boner Law,
sentences.zh: 你知道，他不是那种卡森或史密斯，甚至博纳·劳那样的魅力型演说家，

sentences.en: who's quite a draw because he can fulminate and he's got that stern look about him as well.
sentences.zh: 博纳·劳很有号召力，因为他能慷慨激昂地演说，而且他看起来也很严肃。

sentences.en: No contemporary political campaign gets the numbers out on the streets, like Carson's campaign, which he quickly realises it's no good just speaking to demonstrations in BelfaSt.
sentences.zh: 当时没有任何政治运动能像卡森的运动那样把人们带到街头，他很快意识到仅仅在贝尔法斯特的示威中演讲是不够的。

sentences.en: He needs to go and shift public opinion in Britain, and that's what he spends his time doing throughout 1913 and the first half of 1914.
sentences.zh: 他需要去改变英国的公众舆论，这就是他在1913年和1914年上半年一直忙于做的事情。

sentences.en: But are there two other things, though?
sentences.zh: 但还有另外两件事，不是吗？

sentences.en: One, the Liberals are trapped.
sentences.zh: 第一，自由党人被困住了。

sentences.en: But they rely on the Irish Parliamentary Party, the Irish Nationalists of John Redmond, to whom they've promised home rule.
sentences.zh: 但他们依赖约翰·雷德蒙的爱尔兰议会党，即爱尔兰民族主义者，他们已经向这些人承诺了地方自治。

sentences.en: So they can't welch out of it because then they're sunk.
sentences.zh: 所以他们不能反悔，因为一旦反悔，他们就完了。

sentences.en: Then they lose their majority.
sentences.zh: 那样他们就会失去多数席位。

sentences.en: That's number one.
sentences.zh: 这是第一点。

sentences.en: But number two, because of this, what seems like a very arcane procedural thing, which is the Parliament Act, which means the House of Lords can't scrap your legislation.
sentences.zh: 但第二点，因为这个原因，看起来像是一件非常晦涩的程序性事务，即《议会法案》，这意味着上议院不能废除你们的立法。

sentences.en: They can delay it for two years, can't they?
sentences.zh: 他们可以推迟两年，对吧？

sentences.en: You have to introduce it three times.
sentences.zh: 你必须提交三次。

sentences.en: Because of that, they're stuck on this, you know, what's the expression?
sentences.zh: 正因为如此，他们被困在这个，你知道，怎么说来着？

sentences.en: It's not a treadmill.
sentences.zh: 这不是跑步机。

sentences.en: It's one of those things that-
sentences.zh: 是那种……

sentences.en: Hamster wheel.
sentences.zh: 仓鼠轮。

sentences.en: Hamster wheel.
sentences.zh: 仓鼠轮。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: They're in a hamster wheel.
sentences.zh: 他们被困在仓鼠轮里了。

sentences.en: And it's very Brexit, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这很有脱欧的感觉，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, it is very Brexit.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实很像脱欧。

sentences.en: They're stuck.
sentences.zh: 他们被困住了。

sentences.en: The sense of a ticking clock.
sentences.zh: 那种时钟滴答作响的感觉。

sentences.en: They're stuck.
sentences.zh: 他们被困住了。

sentences.en: But it's a three-year ticking clock, right?
sentences.zh: 但这是一个三年的倒计时，对吧？

sentences.en: And that means that Carson has the best part of two to three years.
sentences.zh: 这意味着卡森有两到三年的黄金时间。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: To go around the country whipping people up, but also presumably to recruit his paramilitary.
sentences.zh: 去全国各地煽动民众，但想必也是为了招募他的准军事部队。

sentences.en: And to get guns.
sentences.zh: 还要搞到枪支。

sentences.en: But Dan, I mean, a thing that a government does when faced by an insurgent paramilitary force is to send the police or failing that, the army in, to suppress them.
sentences.zh: 但是丹，我的意思是，政府在面对叛乱的准军事力量时，通常会派遣警察，如果不行就派军队去镇压他们。

sentences.en: So why don't they do that?
sentences.zh: 那他们为什么不这样做呢？

sentences.en: Well, that would be, I think, firstly, that would be quite a big step.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想首先，那会是相当大的一步。

sentences.en: And the Liberal government in this period are hoping that the Irish home rule can be enacted peacefully.
sentences.zh: 而且这一时期的自由党政府希望爱尔兰地方自治能够和平实现。

sentences.en: They'd rather not have any confrontations.
sentences.zh: 他们宁愿没有任何冲突。

sentences.en: Because, of course, this is a period where there are troops on the streets more often than more or less any other time in the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 因为当然，这是一个军队出现在街头的频率比20世纪任何其他时期都要高的时期。

sentences.en: If you read George Dangerfield's famous book, The Strange Death of Liberal England, particularly confrontations over trade union disputes in 1911, it's quite a febrile atmosphere.
sentences.zh: 如果你读过乔治·丹格菲尔德的名著《自由主义英国的奇异死亡》，特别是1911年工会纠纷引发的对抗，那气氛相当狂热。

sentences.en: And the last thing you want is, you know, having to deal with, you know, striking railwomen in Liverpool or wherever, and then having to send troops to Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 你最不希望看到的就是，在处理利物浦或其他地方的铁路女工罢工的同时，还要派军队去北爱尔兰。

sentences.en: But, of course, as it will play out when we get to 1914, the loyalty of the army, particularly
sentences.zh: 但当然，正如我们在1914年所看到的那样，军队的忠诚度，特别是

sentences.en: its Anglo-Irish officer caste, are absolutely not on board with the idea of enforcing home rule on basically their family and friends in the north of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 其英裔爱尔兰军官阶层，根本不赞成强迫北爱尔兰的家人和朋友接受地方自治的想法。

sentences.en: Or, in fact, in Dublin as well, of course, given that many of those landed families were based in the south of Ireland too.
sentences.zh: 或者实际上在都柏林也是如此，毕竟许多那些地主家庭也居住在爱尔兰南部。

sentences.en: So they couldn't really rely on the army.
sentences.zh: 所以他们真的无法依赖军队。

sentences.en: And this is demonstrated by what's called the Curragh incident, the Curragh mutiny?
sentences.zh: 这通过所谓的“库拉事件”，即“库拉兵变”得到了证明？

sentences.en: The Curragh mutiny, yeah.
sentences.zh: 库拉兵变，是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is how this whole story plays out.
sentences.zh: 所以整个故事就是这样发展的。

sentences.en: The UVF forms in 1913.
sentences.zh: 阿尔斯特志愿军（UVF）成立于1913年。

sentences.en: It very rapidly professionalizes itself.
sentences.zh: 它很快就实现了专业化。

sentences.en: It brings in a retired Indian army general to command it.
sentences.zh: 它请来了一位退役的印度陆军将军来指挥。

sentences.en: It's drilling regularly and so on, but it's short of arMs.
sentences.zh: 它在定期进行操练等等，但缺乏武器。

sentences.en: So it manages through this kind of John Buchan-esque gun running episode, where a ship sails from,
sentences.zh: 所以它通过这种约翰·巴肯式的走私军火事件，一艘船从——

sentences.en: I think it's Denmark, eventually arrives at Larn on the northern Irish coast, importing
sentences.zh: 我想是丹麦出发，最终抵达北爱尔兰海岸的拉恩，进口了

sentences.en: 24,000 rifles, which they purchased from Germany.
sentences.zh: 24000支从德国购买的步枪。

sentences.en: The old Unionists had bought outright, but had to basically spuggle into the country.
sentences.zh: 老联合派已经全额买下，但基本上必须走私进国境。

sentences.en: This is a huge deal at the time.
sentences.zh: 这在当时是一件大事。

sentences.en: And when the army get wind of this at the Curragh camp, which is the main British army base just outside Dublin, many of them make their feelings known to their commanding officer
sentences.zh: 当军队在库拉军营——都柏林郊外主要的英国陆军基地——得知此事时，许多人向他们的指挥官表达了不满，

sentences.en: to say, we won't, we'd rather resign our commissions than be forced to coerce the Unionists in the north into accepting Irish home rule.
sentences.zh: 他们说：我们宁愿辞去军职，也不愿被迫强迫北方的联合派接受爱尔兰地方自治。

sentences.en: What happens then?
sentences.zh: 那后来发生了什么？

sentences.en: The government panic.
sentences.zh: 政府恐慌了。

sentences.en: The army, some of the more kind of loyal, if you want to put it that way, army top brass try and rein these officers in, but they're adamant.
sentences.zh: 军队中一些比较忠诚的高层试图约束这些军官，但他们态度坚决。

sentences.en: Many of them are Anglo-Irish, as I mentioned.
sentences.zh: 正如我提到的，他们许多人是英裔爱尔兰人。

sentences.en: And then there's an enormous demonstration in Hyde Park in London, with about a quarter of a million people who turn out to hear Edward Carson speak in defence of the Curragh
sentences.zh: 随后在伦敦海德公园举行了一场规模巨大的示威，大约有25万人走上街头，听取爱德华·卡森为所谓的“库拉兵变者”辩护。

sentences.en: mutineers, as they're called.
sentences.zh: 大众的观点是，好吧，他们做得完全正确。

sentences.en: The popular opinion is, well, they're doing exactly the right thing.
sentences.zh: 试图将此强加给北爱尔兰是完全不公正的。

sentences.en: This is completely unjust to try and impose this on Northern Ireland.
sentences.zh: 丹，当你提到大众观点时，那是一个在民意调查出现之前的时代。

sentences.en: When you say the popular opinion, Dan, this is an age before opinion polls.
sentences.zh: 我们是否真的了解英国人——我不知道，通过补选或者

sentences.en: Do we actually have a sense of what the British, maybe, I don't know, from by-elections or
sentences.zh: 其他什么方式——英国公众，多数人或多数派会站在哪一边？

sentences.en: whatever, of what the British public, which way they would have, the majority or plurality would have sided?
sentences.zh: 嗯，这基本上就是我在关于这个主题的书中试图探讨的问题，那就是，当时没有民意调查。

sentences.en: Well, this is basically the question that I tried to explore in my book on this topic, which was, there aren't opinion polls.
sentences.zh: 来自普通选民的证据通常很简略。

sentences.en: The kind of, the evidence from ordinary voters is usually sketchy.
sentences.zh: 你通常只能看到那个时期的高层政治记录，我认为这是史学研究中的一个重大空白。

sentences.en: You usually only ever get high political accounts of this period, which I thought was a major gap in the historiography.
sentences.zh: 所以你试图去发现人们当时的感受。

sentences.en: So you try and discover how people were feeling.
sentences.zh: 而你可以观察的方法之一就是那些巨大的示威活动。

sentences.en: And one of the ways you can look at it is the huge demonstrations.
sentences.zh: 卡森在英国各地发表演讲。

sentences.en: And Carson speaks everywhere in Britain.
sentences.zh: 他在因弗内斯、普利茅斯、诺里奇、芒廷阿什、朗达谷、伯明翰演讲，

sentences.en: He speaks in Inverness, in Plymouth, in Norwich, in Mountain Ash, in the Rhonda Valley, in Birmingham,
sentences.zh: 正如你所料，经常在利物浦和格拉斯哥演讲，还有在达勒姆的沃尔森德，在赫恩山自行车馆，汤姆，离荷兰塔不远。

sentences.en: frequently in Liverpool and Glasgow, as you might expect, but in Wall's End, in Durham, at the Hearn Hill, Velodrome, Tom, not far from Holland Towers.
sentences.zh: 他在1914年对一场大规模示威发表了演讲。

sentences.en: He speaks to a mass demonstration in 1914.
sentences.zh: 所以这些活动通常有巨大的参与人数。

sentences.en: So there's a huge, there's usually huge turnout for these events.
sentences.zh: 它们通常高度程式化。

sentences.en: They're often highly stylized.
sentences.zh: 你看过米切尔和肯扬档案馆里那些爱德华时代的纪录片吗？

sentences.en: Have you ever watched the Mitchell and Kenyon archive of kind of Edwardian newsreels?
sentences.zh: 你会看到游行对于爱德华时代的人来说是多么重要，各种不同的群体，宗教、工会等等。

sentences.en: And you see how often processions were a big deal for the Edwardians and various different guys as religious, trade unions, whatever.
sentences.zh: 通常的做法是，会有一场穿过城镇的游行，有点像奥兰治游行，几乎是类似的事情。

sentences.en: The usual deal would be, there'd be a procession through the town, a bit like an orange march, almost similar sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 或者卡森的马车会被卸下马匹，忠诚的支持者会拉着他在城里走。

sentences.en: Or Carson's carriage would be unhorsed and loyal supporters would pull him through the town.
sentences.zh: 所以他能把大量的人带到街上。

sentences.en: So he gets huge numbers out onto the street.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，自由党政府在补选中节节败退，输给了以这个纲领进行竞选的联合派。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the Liberal government are losing by-elections left, right and centre to unionists who are campaigning on this platform.
sentences.zh: 所以丹，军队有——军队的某些部分似乎发生了兵变。

sentences.en: So Dan, the army has, elements of the army seem to mutinate.
sentences.zh: 到处都是游行，人们在操练。

sentences.en: There are all these processions, there are people drilling.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅仅是阿尔斯特的志愿军。

sentences.en: So there's not just the volunteers in Ulster.
sentences.zh: 我想在1913年还成立了一个竞争对手——爱尔兰志愿军。

sentences.en: There's been a rival group of Irish volunteers that has been formed, I think, in 1913.
sentences.zh: 还有关于人们在英国招募、在英国签署盟约的传闻。

sentences.en: There's also talk of people recruiting in Britain, people signing covenants in Britain.
sentences.zh: 问题是，乔治——我说的是乔治五世，他是《历史的余味》的好朋友，顶级的国王——他在做什么？

sentences.en: And the question is, what's George, I said, George V, very much a friend of the rest is history, top king, what's he doing?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他一定在想，天哪，我的联合王国，你知道，正走向毁灭的边缘。

sentences.en: I mean, he must be thinking, geez, my United Kingdom is, you know, heading for the knackers yard.
sentences.zh: 国王被这件事吓坏了。

sentences.en: The king is massively spooked by this.
sentences.zh: 国王被这件事吓坏了。

sentences.en: And of course, he's had a tough early period of his reign because he was going to be forced to flood the House of Lords with liberal peers, of course, at the height of the people's
sentences.zh: 当然，他统治初期的日子并不好过，因为他被迫要在人民预算辩论达到高潮时，向议会上议院塞进一批自由派贵族，

sentences.en: budget debate, which I think you've touched on already.
sentences.zh: 我想你之前已经提到过这一点了。

sentences.en: But George V intervenes in politics.
sentences.zh: 但乔治五世介入了政治。

sentences.en: He calls the Buckingham Palace Conference in July 1914 to try and get the key players around the table to try and thrash out some sort of compromise.
sentences.zh: 他在1914年7月召开了白金汉宫会议，试图让各方关键人物坐到谈判桌前，商讨出某种妥协方案。

sentences.en: But of course, the Irish nationalists are not willing to compromise.
sentences.zh: 但当然，爱尔兰民族主义者并不愿意妥协。

sentences.en: And they still see the island of Ireland as a single political unit, and they're not prepared.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然将爱尔兰岛视为一个单一的政治实体，对此他们毫无准备。

sentences.en: But Dan, this is happening in July 1914, and they're having to have a conference to discuss what to do about Ireland.
sentences.zh: 但丹，这可是1914年7月发生的事，他们竟然还得开会讨论如何处理爱尔兰问题。

sentences.en: But I thought the Home Rule Bill has already passed, hasn't it?
sentences.zh: 我以为《自治法案》已经通过了，不是吗？

sentences.en: So why are they still discussing it?
sentences.zh: 那为什么他们还在讨论它？

sentences.en: Tom, I don't want to terrify the listeners, but we've actually given them a very, very
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我不想吓唬听众，但我们实际上给他们讲的是一个非常、非常

sentences.en: simplified version of the story.
sentences.zh: 简化的版本。

sentences.en: It's even more complex.
sentences.zh: 情况要复杂得多。

sentences.en: Well, because the bill had passed in May 1914.
sentences.zh: 嗯，因为法案是在1914年5月通过的。

sentences.en: I think that's right, isn't it, Dan?
sentences.zh: 我想那是对的，对吧，丹？

sentences.en: The bill had passed in May.
sentences.zh: 法案是在5月通过的。

sentences.en: But even at that point, the Aswith government are still dithering about what to do with it.
sentences.zh: 但即使在那时，阿斯奎斯政府对于如何处理它仍然犹豫不决。

sentences.en: They are talking about excluding part of Ulster.
sentences.zh: 他们正在讨论将阿尔斯特的一部分排除在外。

sentences.en: But the question now is, are they going to exclude a bit of it?
sentences.zh: 但现在的问题是，他们是要排除其中的一小部分吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to exclude the whole province?
sentences.zh: 他们是要排除整个省吗？

sentences.en: Are they going to exclude nine counties, six, maybe even three counties?
sentences.zh: 他们是要排除九个郡、六个郡，甚至可能只是三个郡？

sentences.en: And does that mean they're going to sell out, in Carsten's view, all the unionists?
sentences.zh: 这是否意味着在卡森看来，他们要出卖所有的统一派人士？

sentences.en: And I mean, he's still holding out for no Home Rule at all.
sentences.zh: 而且我的意思是，他仍然坚持完全不要自治。

sentences.en: OK, but what do the Irish Parliamentary Party think about this?
sentences.zh: 好吧，那爱尔兰议会党对此有何看法？

sentences.en: Because they've been promised Home Rule.
sentences.zh: 因为他们已经得到了自治的承诺。

sentences.en: The bill has passed.
sentences.zh: 法案已经通过了。

sentences.en: And it's still not being instituted.
sentences.zh: 但它仍然没有被实施。

sentences.en: So what's their take on this?
sentences.zh: 那么他们对此有何看法？

sentences.en: The leadership under John Redmond at the time, the Irish Nationalist Party leader, he is adamant, understandably, I think, from his perspective,
sentences.zh: 当时的领导层，即爱尔兰民族党领袖约翰·雷德蒙，他非常坚定，我认为从他的角度来看是可以理解的，

sentences.en: that Ireland is a political unit that can't be dismembered, as he would describe it, and needs to be granted Home Rule on a 32-county basis.
sentences.zh: 他认为爱尔兰是一个不可分割的政治实体，正如他所描述的那样，需要以32个郡为基础获得自治权。

sentences.en: And he's not prepared to concede ground to the Ulster Unionists, no matter how much they're recruiting to the UVF.
sentences.zh: 无论阿尔斯特志愿军招募了多少人，他都不准备向阿尔斯特统一派让步。

sentences.en: Maybe there's a sense that John Redmond underestimates the vehemence of their opposition, you kind of expect that once it's passed through Parliament, then it will happen.
sentences.zh: 也许有人觉得约翰·雷德蒙低估了他们反对的激烈程度，你本以为一旦法案在议会通过，事情就会发生。

sentences.en: The Liberal government will ensure it will happen.
sentences.zh: 自由党政府会确保它发生。

sentences.en: But it just doesn't, though, because it stands on a knife edge.
sentences.zh: 但它就是没发生，因为它处于千钧一发之际。

sentences.en: There's kind of real brinkmanship in this period about how is this going to play out?
sentences.zh: 这一时期确实存在真正的边缘政策，这到底会如何收场？

sentences.en: Because, as Dominic touched on before, not only have we had the Ulster Covenant, we've had the British Covenant as well.
sentences.zh: 因为正如多米尼克之前提到的，我们不仅有《阿尔斯特盟约》，还有《英国盟约》。

sentences.en: And it's claimed in some circles that two million people sign the British Covenant in Britain.
sentences.zh: 据某些圈子声称，有两百万人签署了英国的《英国盟约》。

sentences.en: This is outside of Ireland.
sentences.zh: 这还是在爱尔兰之外。

sentences.en: People are openly joining UVF-style groups in Glasgow and London and Liverpool and are willing to go and defend Ulster in the event of violence.
sentences.zh: 人们公开加入格拉斯哥、伦敦和利物浦的阿尔斯特志愿军式组织，并愿意在发生暴力事件时保卫阿尔斯特。

sentences.en: Is it fair to say that by July 1914, the government is faced with large numbers of people in Ulster
sentences.zh: 说1914年7月时，政府正面临阿尔斯特和

sentences.en: and across Britain who are prepared to resort to violence in defence, certainly, of Ulster, staying British, not being subjected to home rule as they would see it.
